definition: Dispersion between repeated IC50 measurements of the same standardised compound, in pIC50 log units, directly comparable with a model RMSE.

noise_floor.recommended_basis: pooled_within_compound_sd_differing_under_1_log: the pooled SD over replicate groups that actually differ (identical re-reports excluded) and that agree to within one log unit. This is the dispersion of genuinely repeated measurement of the same chemistry, and is the number a model RMSE should be compared with.
noise_floor.ceiling_basis: pooled_within_compound_sd_differing_groups: the same quantity over every differing group, including the ones whose replicates disagree by several log units. Those are contradictory measurements rather than noise around a value, so this is a ceiling on how generous the floor could honestly be made.

all_groups_figure_and_why_it_is_not_used.reason: The pooled SD over all replicate groups mixes two populations: identical re-reports contribute zero variance and deflate it, while irreconcilable groups inflate it. It is reported for completeness and is not a defensible noise floor in either direction.

caveats: These are repeated literature and patent reports, not a designed replicate experiment: they mix assay protocols, so none of these figures is pure assay noise.

The spread distribution is bimodal: most groups are identical re-reports of one number, and a long tail disagrees by several log units. The mean spread (and the pooled SD over all groups) sits between the two modes and describes neither; the histogram above is the honest summary.
Only replicated compounds contribute. 3489 of 3965 curated compounds are measured once, so the floor is measured on 12.0% of the curated set.

The recommended figure is conditional dispersion for differing repeat groups with spread <=1 log unit, not an unconditional lower bound on held-out RMSE. Predictions target compound medians, not individual reports; the repeated subset may differ from the test population. A lower RMSE alone does not prove leakage or memorisation. Independence of these reports has not been established.
